circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009, designed by renowned circuit architect Hermann Tilke. As the second Middle Eastern F1 venue to be built after Bahrain, it preceded later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia to the calendar.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Melbourne's Albert Park Circuit is a street course that winds around Albert Park Lake in the city's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting racing categories. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and serves as a regular fixture on the international motorsport calendar.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following extensive modifications and a name change, the track returned to hosting the grand prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The venue hosted its first F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race in the Middle East that same year. Beyond its annual Formula One Grand Prix, the facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2, drag racing, and endurance competitions, while holding a FIA Grade 1 license and offering multiple track configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse mix of straights and corners that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has hosted Formula One racing since 1950 and became a permanent fixture on the championship calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006. The venue is renowned as the traditional home of the Belgian Grand Prix and represents one of motorsport's oldest racing facilities, having operated continuously since the 1920s.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its role in Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese racing venue has predominantly hosted the Chinese Grand Prix since 2004, with a gap in competition from 2020 to 2023 before resuming in 2024. The facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near the Northamptonshire villages of Silverstone and Whittlebury, this English racing venue inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race two years later. After alternating with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades, the championship event became a permanent fixture at the circuit from 1987 onwards, while the track also accommodates the British MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One venue held behind the Iron Curtain when it hosted its inaugural Grand Prix in 1986, commemorating Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál. Built in just eight months near a major highway outside the capital, this 4. 381 km circuit was constructed faster than any other Formula One track, after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's largest park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing venue constructed in 1922 near Milan, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built circuit and only the third of its kind globally. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, with a single interruption in 1980 for renovation, the track earns its "Temple of Speed" reputation through its characteristic long straights and fast-cornering sections.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland and hosting a crowd capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is internationally renowned as a prestigious host of Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course weaving through Paradise, Nevada, that follows the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares. The track passes by iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere entertainment complex.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has been home to Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015, though it previously hosted the championship race on a different configuration during two earlier periods, with the most recent visit occurring in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist Formula One architects, the track was built specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the championship calendar beginning in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, hugging the harbor of this small principality. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, the track is popularly called "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that district's boundaries.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Nestled in the Dutch coastal dunes 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259-kilometer track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining Formula One in 2021. The partnership between the circuit and the sport concluded in 2026, ending the revival of the iconic national race at this seaside venue.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha near Lusail, this 5. 419-kilometer racing venue features a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later named after Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident in 1977. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features associated facilities including a karting venue dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021, while also accommodating international electric racing events from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its street-based racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse mix of straights and corners that test multiple aspects of driver skill. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The venue regularly hosts multiple motorsport disciplines including MotoGP, NASCAR, and endurance racing competitions, while having previously accommodated various other series such as IndyCar and American Le Mans racing.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has captured two world championships during his 23-season career while recording 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans 24 Hours triumphs with Toyota, making him the sole competitor to win both an F1 drivers' title and the World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed six victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as part of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during 2019 and 2020 while previously competing for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver who races in the European Le Mans Series within the LMP2 category while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One. The Melbourne-born competitor has appeared in seven Formula One races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One, having previously achieved a career highlight when he secured victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has achieved a record-tying seven world championships, matching Michael Schumacher's total. He holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, while his endurance racing accomplishments include winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a racing driver from New Zealand, currently races in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW and part-time in NASCAR. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship whilst racing for McLaren, accumulating 13 Grand Prix victories over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. He previously achieved success with Alpine, securing a race victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing over 15 seasons of experience to the grid. A six-time Grand Prix winner, Pérez achieved his best championship result in 2023 when he finished second in the drivers' standings while racing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver currently racing for McLaren, has secured nine Formula One victories over his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. After a brief Formula One career spanning 2023 to 2024, he has transitioned to sports car racing, including previous involvement with Era Motorsport in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently fulfilling a reserve role across Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He previously competed as a full-time driver in the championship between 2021 and 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. He has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He continues to hold the distinction of being the only Chinese driver to have competed at the highest level of motorsport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base since 2021, this French works team adopted the Alpine brand name to represent Renault's sports car division following its previous identity as Renault F1 Team. The squad maintained factory backing throughout its tenure until the automotive manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One multiple times throughout the sport's history. The squad currently competes under the AMR GP Limited banner as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, has been a cornerstone of Formula One since the championship's inception in 1950 and remains the sport's most successful and longest-running team. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the Maranello-based outfit has achieved unparalleled longevity by competing in every season of the World Championship.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-based Formula One team founded by Gene Haas and debuting in 2016, the outfit competes under the TGR Haas F1 Team banner. Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had led the organization since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Peter Sauber's Swiss engineering and racing outfit operated as an independent Formula One constructor from 1993 until its exit in 2025, becoming the sport's fourth-longest-serving team by race starts. Prior to joining the grid, the organization established itself in endurance racing with two world championships and a 1989 Le Mans victory. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the technical and competitive foundation for its Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One constructor headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, with primary ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company. The team competes in the sport under its current commercial partnership branding arrangement.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, is headquartered in Brackley and races under a German licence, with ownership shared equally among Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff as of January 2022. The marque's racing identity is historically associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Red Bull Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but operating under an Austrian license, emerged in 2005 as part of Red Bull GmbH's Formula One portfolio alongside Racing Bulls. Under Christian Horner's leadership from inception through 2024, the team became a dominant force in the sport, with Laurent Mekies taking over as principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based at a sprawling Grove facility in Oxfordshire, the team has maintained its status as both competitor and constructor throughout its operation.
